title: Getting started with hazrd
text: package ships simulated survival dataset, test_data. three required columns phs (continuous score), age (time event censoring), status (event indicator: 1 = event, 0 = censored). test data included package.

title: Getting started with hazrd
text: phs_metrics() single entry point discrimination statistics. fits Cox proportional hazards model derives metrics fit. metrics argument controls statistics computed; column names passed strings default "phs", "age", "status".

what: All core metrics in one call
title: Getting started with hazrd
text: returned tibble one row per metric. conf_low, conf_high, se NA bootstrapping enabled.
code: metrics <- phs_metrics(   test_data,   metrics  = c("HR", "C_index", "OR", "HR_SD"),   or_age   = 70 ) metrics #> # A tibble: 4 × 9 #>   metric      estimate conf_low conf_high    se n_numerator n_denominator method #>   <chr>          <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl>       <int>         <int> <chr>  #> 1 HR[80-100]…    8.17        NA        NA    NA         200           200 conti… #> 2 C_index        0.708       NA        NA    NA          NA            NA harre… #> 3 HR_SD          2.12        NA        NA    NA          NA            NA NA     #> 4 OR[80-100]…    8.52        NA        NA    NA         200           200 NA     #> # ℹ 1 more variable: adjusted <lgl>

title: Getting started with hazrd
text: default phs_metrics() computes HR[80-100]_[0-20] — ratio top 20% bottom 20% PHS distribution. Use hr_numerator / hr_denominator change bands: multiple HRs one call, supply hr_pairs:
code: phs_metrics(test_data, metrics = "HR", hr_numerator = 0.90, hr_denominator = 0.10) #> # A tibble: 1 × 9 #>   metric      estimate conf_low conf_high    se n_numerator n_denominator method #>   <chr>          <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl>       <int>         <int> <chr>  #> 1 HR[90-100]…     13.7       NA        NA    NA         100           100 conti… #> # ℹ 1 more variable: adjusted <lgl> phs_metrics(   test_data,   metrics  = "HR",   hr_pairs = list(     list(numerator = c(0.80, 1.00), denominator = c(0.00, 0.20)),     list(numerator = c(0.80, 1.00), denominator = c(0.40, 0.60))   ) ) #> # A tibble: 2 × 9 #>   metric      estimate conf_low conf_high    se n_numerator n_denominator method #>   <chr>          <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl>       <int>         <int> <chr>  #> 1 HR[80-100]…     8.17       NA        NA    NA         200           200 conti… #> 2 HR[80-100]…     3.05       NA        NA    NA         200           200 conti… #> # ℹ 1 more variable: adjusted <lgl>

title: Getting started with hazrd
text: computed Kaplan-Meier survival estimates specific age. or_age accepts vector; one row returned per age:
code: phs_metrics(test_data, metrics = "OR", or_age = c(65, 70, 75)) #> # A tibble: 3 × 9 #>   metric      estimate conf_low conf_high    se n_numerator n_denominator method #>   <chr>          <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl>       <int>         <int> <chr>  #> 1 OR[80-100]…     8.22       NA        NA    NA         200           200 NA     #> 2 OR[80-100]…     8.52       NA        NA    NA         200           200 NA     #> 3 OR[80-100]…    19.1        NA        NA    NA         200           200 NA     #> # ℹ 1 more variable: adjusted <lgl>

title: Getting started with hazrd
text: Set bootstrap = TRUE populate conf_low, conf_high, se. Use small n_boot speed development:
code: phs_metrics(   test_data,   metrics   = c("HR", "C_index", "HR_SD"),   bootstrap = TRUE,   n_boot    = 300,   seed      = 42 ) #> # A tibble: 3 × 9 #>   metric     estimate conf_low conf_high     se n_numerator n_denominator method #>   <chr>         <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>  <dbl>       <int>         <int> <chr>  #> 1 HR[80-100…    8.17     5.93     11.8   1.36           200           200 conti… #> 2 C_index       0.708    0.680     0.734 0.0139          NA            NA harre… #> 3 HR_SD         2.12     1.90      2.42  0.124           NA            NA NA     #> # ℹ 1 more variable: adjusted <lgl>

title: Getting started with hazrd
text: Column names passed strings, making phs_metrics() straightforward use non-standard data frames:
code: test_data2 <- with(test_data, data.frame(   score     = phs,   diagnosis_age = age,   case      = status ))  phs_metrics(   test_data2,   phs   = "score",   time  = "diagnosis_age",   event = "case",   metrics = c("HR", "C_index") ) #> # A tibble: 2 × 9 #>   metric      estimate conf_low conf_high    se n_numerator n_denominator method #>   <chr>          <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> <dbl>       <int>         <int> <chr>  #> 1 HR[80-100]…    8.17        NA        NA    NA         200           200 conti… #> 2 C_index        0.708       NA        NA    NA          NA            NA harre… #> # ℹ 1 more variable: adjusted <lgl>

title: Getting started with hazrd
text: phs_km_curve() stratifies cohort percentile bands plots empirical Kaplan-Meier survival curves band. returns either ggplot object (output = "plot", default) tidy data frame (output = "data").

title: Getting started with hazrd
text: default intervals produce four bands — top 5% (0.95–1), top 20% (0.80–1), middle 40% (0.30–0.70), bottom 20% (0–0.20). Bands may overlap, useful showing progressively broader high-risk groups compare low-risk reference:
code: phs_km_curve(test_data) #> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_ribbon()`).

title: Getting started with hazrd
text: Pass list c(lo, hi) percentile pairs intervals. Bands can overlap freely — independent Kaplan-Meier fit corresponding subset:
code: phs_km_curve(   test_data,   intervals = list(c(0.95, 1), c(0.80, 1), c(0.00, 0.20)) ) #> Warning: Removed 1 row containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_ribbon()`).

title: Getting started with hazrd
text: non-overlapping bands, use breaks intervals = NULL. Pass numeric vector percentile cutpoints (strictly 0 1):
code: # Quintiles phs_km_curve(test_data, intervals = NULL, breaks = c(0.20, 0.40, 0.60, 0.80)) #> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_ribbon()`).

title: Getting started with hazrd
text: phs_km_curve() returns standard ggplot object can extended ggplot2 layers, themes, scales:
code: phs_km_curve(test_data) +   labs(     title = "Disease-free Survival by PHS Percentile",     x     = "Age (years)",     y     = "Disease-free Probability",     color = "PHS Group",     fill  = "PHS Group"   ) +   coord_cartesian(xlim = c(40, 100)) #> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_ribbon()`).

title: Getting started with hazrd
text: Use output = "data" want build fully custom plot pass survival estimates analysis: returned data frame columns time, estimate, conf.low, conf.high, n.risk, n.event, stratum, can used directly ggplot2:
code: km_data <- phs_km_curve(test_data, output = "data") head(km_data) #>       time  estimate  conf.low conf.high n.risk n.event stratum #> 1 44.30748 1.0000000 1.0000000 1.0000000     51       0 95-100% #> 2 47.04070 0.9800000 0.9419529 1.0000000     50       1 95-100% #> 3 48.14581 0.9800000 0.9419529 1.0000000     49       0 95-100% #> 4 48.58741 0.9595833 0.9062444 1.0000000     48       1 95-100% #> 5 51.75902 0.9391667 0.8747578 1.0000000     47       1 95-100% #> 6 52.01547 0.9187500 0.8454998 0.9983463     46       1 95-100% ggplot(km_data, aes(x = time, y = estimate,                     ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high,                     color = stratum, fill = stratum)) +   geom_ribbon(alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +   geom_step(linewidth = 0.8) +   scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1", name = "PHS Group") +   scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1", name = "PHS Group") +   coord_cartesian(xlim = c(40, 100), ylim = c(0, 1)) +   labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Disease-free Probability") +   theme_minimal() #> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_ribbon()`).

title: Getting started with hazrd
text: phs_cox_curve() fits Cox proportional-hazards model (phs sole predictor) returns predicted survival curves individuals specified PHS percentiles. Unlike phs_km_curve(), smooth model-based predictions, empirical group estimates.  Supply specific percentiles via percentiles argument:
code: phs_cox_curve(test_data) phs_cox_curve(test_data, percentiles = c(0.01, 0.10, 0.50, 0.90, 0.99))

title: Getting started with hazrd
text: phs_abs_risk() computes absolute (cumulative incidence) risk curves percentile-stratified groups. default method = "km" plots 1 minus Kaplan-Meier survival estimate percentage scale. competing risks present, method = "aalen_johansen" uses Aalen-Johansen estimator. intervals argument works exactly like phs_km_curve() — default four bands (top 5%, top 20%, middle 40%, bottom 20%) used intervals omitted:
code: phs_abs_risk(test_data) #> Warning: Removed 2 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_ribbon()`).

title: Getting started with hazrd
code: phs_abs_risk(   test_data,   intervals = list(c(0.80, 1), c(0.00, 0.20)) ) #> Warning: Removed 1 row containing missing values or values outside the scale range #> (`geom_ribbon()`).

what: Getting estimates at specific time points
title: Getting started with hazrd
text: Use output = "data" time_points extract tidy table estimates specific ages — useful reporting absolute risk clinically meaningful time points:

title: Getting started with hazrd
text: Use phs_risk_table() build numbers--risk strip standalone ggplot, combine curve plot using attach_risk_table() patchwork directly. keeps objects editable ggplots can customise independently combining. publication-ready plots, build customise object separately, combine. time_points argument controls ages columns appear:
code: # Quick usage: let attach_risk_table() build the table from the data p <- phs_abs_risk(test_data) attach_risk_table(p, test_data) library(patchwork)  p  <- phs_abs_risk(test_data) rt <- phs_risk_table(test_data, time_points = c(55, 65, 75, 85))  p / rt + plot_layout(heights = c(3, 1))

text: repository R package named hazrd focused evaluating visualizing polygenic hazard scores (PHS) using survival models. Key components live R/ directory tests use testthat/. Files scan first - R/phs_metrics.R — user-facing metric orchestrator (HR, C-index, ) - R/metrics-internal.R — metric implementations (._calc_* functions) - R/bootstrap-internal.R — bootstrapping orchestration; uses boot::boot - R/create_lookup.R — generation per-percentile K-M predictions - tests/testthat/ — unit tests validate behavior - DESCRIPTION, NAMESPACE, README.Rmd — packaging install metadata - Never edit README.md directly — auto-generated knitting README.Rmd via rmarkdown::render(). Always use Docker container pandoc: docker run --rm -v /path//hazrd:/repo -r-image \       Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("/repo/README.Rmd", output_file = "/repo/README.md")' use knitr::knit() — lacks pandoc emits YAML frontmatter literal text output. - docs/specs/spec-sheet.md — package spec sheet (may local/ignored; ask maintainer copy) Big-picture architecture & data flow - Input: data.frame minimum phs, age (time) status (event). - phs_metrics() single primary entry-point computing metrics; fits Cox model (survival::coxph) derives metrics fit. - Metric calculation split: point estimates computed first; bootstrap = TRUE package calls .run_bootstrap() re-fits model resamples derives bootstrap CIs using boot::boot + boot.ci. - Outputs tidy tibbles canonical columns: metric, estimate, conf_low, conf_high, se, n_numerator, n_denominator, method, adjusted. Developer spec - See docs/specs/spec-sheet.md canonical package specification. NOTE: file may kept locally git-ignored maintainer. find repo, ask maintainer provide Markdown copy. spec documents package goals, input conventions (string column names), metric naming conventions (e.g. HR[80-100]_[0-20]), bootstrap behavior (internal boot::boot usage CI methods), worked examples phs_metrics, phs_km, phs_abs_risk. Project-specific conventions & patterns (important edits) - Column names usually passed strings (e.g. phs = "phs", time = "age", event = "status"). Functions accept string names often index data data[[phs]] rather non-standard-eval. - HR metric naming convention literal parsed elsewhere: e.g. HR[80-100]_[0-20] — tests bootstrapping rely exact names align CI results back rows. - Bootstrapping: parallel argument present "" implemented (see .run_bootstrap() guard). Avoid changing parallel semantics without updating guard tests. - Many internal helpers return tibbles canonical column order; keep contract adding new metrics. Build / test / debug workflows (commands can run locally) - Install dev version: R: devtools::install("/path//hazrd") devtools::build() install.packages(..., repos = NULL, type = "source"). - Run package tests: R: devtools::test() shell: R -e ‘devtools::test()’ - Run R CMD check: repo root: R CMD check –-cran . - repo GitHub Action R-CMD-check.yaml (see badge README.md) — mimic action’s R versions reproducing CI locally. Integration points & external deps - Declared imports DESCRIPTION: boot, dplyr, ggplot2, survival, tibble, tidyr, scales. Use consistent idioms. - boot::boot boot::boot.ci central — changes bootstrap interface must preserve numeric-vector contract used boot. Testing & safety notes code changes - Add unit tests tests/testthat/ change metric logic bootstrap behavior. package uses testthat edition 3. - Keep reported metric names stable: tests bootstrap matching rely exact metric name strings. - modifying exported functions, update roxygen comments R/ source — run devtools::document() regenerate NAMESPACE man/ files. - Never use \% roxygen #' comments — backslash doubles generated Rd (\\%), % starts Rd comment can corrupt \arguments{} block. Use plain text (e.g. “percent” “0-20”) instead.

title: Polygenic Hazard Score with Cox Proportional Hazards Model
code: library(hazrd)  # Compute HR, C-index, OR, and HR_SD in one call phs_metrics(   test_data,   metrics = c("HR", "C_index", "OR", "HR_SD"),   or_age  = 70)  # Bootstrapped confidence intervals phs_metrics(   test_data,   metrics   = c("HR", "C_index"),   bootstrap = TRUE,   n_boot    = 999,   seed      = 42 )  # Kaplan-Meier plot — default overlapping intervals phs_km_curve(test_data)  # Overlapping intervals — top 5%, top 20%, bottom 20% phs_km_curve(test_data, intervals = list(c(0.95, 1), c(0.80, 1), c(0, 0.20)))  # Cumulative incidence (absolute risk) curves phs_abs_risk(test_data)  # Absolute risk at specific time points as a tidy table phs_abs_risk(test_data, time_points = c(60, 70, 80), output = "data")  # Numbers-at-risk table combined with the curve p <- phs_abs_risk(test_data) attach_risk_table(p, test_data)  # Legacy exclusive bands via breaks km_data <- phs_km_curve(test_data, intervals = NULL, breaks = c(0.20, 0.40, 0.60, 0.80), output = "data")

title: Polygenic Hazard Score with Cox Proportional Hazards Model

Contributions welcome. phs_percentile() — compute percentile ranks; optionally relative reference population via ref_data phs_cut() — assign individuals percentile strata human-readable factor labels phs_describe() — descriptive statistics (n, events, median follow-, PHS mean/SD) stratum phs_calibration() — calibration plot Hosmer-Lemeshow statistic theme_phs() / scale_color_phs() — default ggplot2 theme colour scale hazrd plots Uno’s C-index — IPCW-weighted concordance heavily censored data (cindex_method = "uno" phs_metrics()) Parallel bootstrap — parallel = "multicore" / "snow" via boot::boot() (argument exists; "" currently active) Alternative HR methods — continuous_point categorical (hr_method argument phs_metrics(); stubs exist)

Options "HR", "C_index", "HR_SD", "". hr_method method use HR calculation. One "continuous_group" (default), "continuous_point", "categorical". "continuous_group" currently implemented. hr_numerator numeric. lower boundary numerator group percentile (e.g., 0.80 top 20%). numerator group defined [hr_numerator, 1.0]. Ignored hr_pairs provided. title: hazrd 0.2.2
text: New phs_abs_risk() function — cumulative incidence (absolute risk) curves stratified PHS percentile group. Supports method = "km" (1 - KM estimate) method = "aalen_johansen" (Aalen-Johansen competing-risk estimator). Returns either ggplot object tidy data frame. Addresses issue #20. strata argument controls percentile grouping via named presets ("quantile_2" "quantile_5", "classic"); custom_cuts accepts arbitrary numeric vector cutpoints. output = "data" time_points supplied, returned tibble one row per stratum x time_point. method = "fine_gray" stubbed error informative message implemented. phs_km_curve() now implements risk_table argument — risk_table = TRUE output = "plot", numbers--risk strip attached curve using patchwork package (added Suggests). Falls back warning plain plot patchwork installed. Addresses issue #49. phs_abs_risk() also supports risk_table = TRUE identical behavior phs_km_curve().

title: hazrd 0.2.1
text: phs_km_curve(): new intervals parameter accepts list c(lo, hi) percentile pairs, enabling overlapping KM strata (e.g. top 5%, top 20%, bottom 20%). Default produces four bands: 0.95-1, 0.80-1, 0.30-0.70, 0-0.20. legacy breaks parameter retained backward compatibility.

title: hazrd 0.2.1

title: hazrd 0.2.1
text: Vignette updated overlapping intervals examples breaks legacy usage. README installation section updated use devtools::install_github(); dev-branch instructions added (@dev). NEWS.md corrected: function name phs_km -> phs_km_curve, stale preset list removed, phs_cox_curve entry added.

title: hazrd 0.2.0
text: phs_metrics() — single entry point discrimination metrics (HR, C-index, , HR_SD). Returns tidy tibble one row per metric. Supports built-bootstrapping via boot::boot() "percentile", "bca", "normal" CI methods. phs_km_curve() — Kaplan-Meier curves stratified PHS percentile group. Returns ggplot object default (output = "plot") tidy data frame (output = "data"). Accepts intervals list overlapping strata (e.g. 95–100 %, 80–100 %) breaks vector exclusive bins. Supports ref_data argument train/validation percentile workflows. phs_cox_curve() — Cox model-based survival curves specified PHS percentiles. Fits Cox PH model phs sole predictor returns smooth predicted curves user-supplied percentile values. Supports ref_data train/validation workflows.
